text:
Sam: Heads-up — reproduced a weird throughput drop on the 8xA100 cluster when LL128 is enabled. Looks like the first few forward iterations block on allreduce during KV cache warmup.

Anya: ugh. Which workload + sequence lengths? any traces?

Sam: running LL/TP mixed model (tp=2, tp microbatching on) with long runs of 1024 tokens. Baseline (proto=LL) steady. With proto=LL128 we see 20-40% lower throughput for ~10 steps, then recovers.

Mike: can you paste the perf counters? even a tiny timeline helps.

Sam: paste below (trimmed):

```
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO

iter 1 allreduce latency: 12.2 ms
iter 2 allreduce latency: 9.8 ms
iter 3 allreduce latency: 10.1 ms
iter 10 allreduce latency: 2.4 ms

KV cache miss rate: 95% -> 5% after 8 steps
Batch size per GPU: 4
```

Lee: sounds like early-step backpressure. LL128 uses different NIC packetization and more concurrent channels — could be channel startup overhead + small-msg inefficiency during warmup.

Anya: were you using continuous batching / request coalescing? that changes the message size distribution at step 0.

Sam: yes, continuous batching enabled. We batch small priming requests together, which should help, but trace shows many tiny allreduces when KV warms and we evict/prime prefixes.

perf-bot: Profiling job #kvc-warmup-2053 completed — flamegraph: https://perf.internal/jobs/2053/flamegraph.html (shows heavy time in ncclAllReduce -> transport_ring_send)

Mike: try forcing NCCL_PROTO=LL and compare. Also try upping NCCL_MIN_NRINGS or reducing NCCL_NTHREADS? (not sure param names off top of head)

Lee: experiment idea: disable LL128 for small message sizes only. We have a proto selector shim that can pick by bytes. Patch below (pseudo):

```
if (msg_bytes < 64*1024) proto = LL; else proto = LL128;
```

Anya: that would match intuition — LL for tiny, LL128 for bulk. Do we have telemetry to pick threshold automatically?

Sam: not yet. Manual probe: set NCCL_PROTO=LL then rerun -> allreduce latency steady ~2.3ms from iter 1, throughput stable. So LL128 is the regression surface.

Mike: any HW difference across nodes? PCIe gen / IB link speed? LL128 relies on higher concurrency; bad per-link MTU or QP setup can amplify startup cost.

Sam: nodes identical, IB 100G, MTU 4096. I also tried NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=mlx5_0 -> no change.

perf-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: /artifacts/2053/nccl_traces.tar.gz

Lee: another knob: reduce channel count at startup so fewer tiny messages are split across channels. Env var: NCCL_MAX_RINGS=2 (try)

Sam: ran NCCL_MAX_RINGS=2 + proto=LL128 -> first-step allreduce dropped from 12.2ms -> 6.1ms, still higher than LL but much improved. Nice find.

Anya: good. So two levers: proto fallback for small bytes, or limit rings early and ramp up after kv warmup. We could add a runtime warmup policy: start with conservative nccl config and switch after epoch N.

Mike: does the runtime have a fast switch for NCCL envs? changing envs requires re-init.

Lee: we can reinitialize communicator between warmup and steady state — small overhead but maybe acceptable if done once per session. Or maintain two comm pools and route based on step.

Sam: quick test: keep 2-ring comm pool for first 8 steps then swap to full 8-ring pool. Overhead: ~40ms on swap, but saves overall 15% for those sessions with heavy priming.

Anya: nice. Could we instead detect kv miss-rate and trigger the swap dynamically? that would be more robust.

Sam: yes, runtime exposes kvcache.stats.miss_rate. I'll try a prototype: swap when miss_rate < 0.2 or after 10 steps whichever first.

perf-bot: scheduled perf run 2053b with dynamic swap. Results will be posted to https://perf.internal/jobs/2053b

Mike: long-term, prefer a proto-selector that picks per-allreduce based on msg size. No communicator swap complexity.

Lee: agreed. But quick win is the dynamic comm pool ramp because it's low-risk and doesn't require kernel-level proto selection.

Sam: action items:
- Sam: land dynamic comm-pool prototype and run cluster-wide perf tests (WIP)
- Anya: add telemetry for per-allreduce msg_bytes histogram
- Mike: experiment with NCCL_MAX_RINGS ramp schedule and get numbers
- Lee: draft patch for proto-bytes selector (pseudo above)

Sam: thanks everyone. I'll post the perf run link when complete. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued: internal/runtime/comm-pools/v1 -> staging (triggered by Sam)

Sam: quick note — if anyone else is triaging LL128 issues, check job 2053 for reference.
